key_insight: A PEDOT:PSS/graphene/n-Si trilayer combines improved photovoltaic efficiency with graphene-mediated protection against ambient degradation.
engineering_relevance: The architecture offers a route to more efficient, environmentally stable Schottky solar cells on untextured silicon.
method: Benchmark planar trilayer cells against graphene/n-Si and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si references.
Use PEDOT:PSS for anti-reflection, moderate graphene p-doping, and improved conductivity.
Use graphene as a charge-transport interface and impermeable protective barrier.
evidence_signal: The trilayer achieved 8.52% PCE versus 4.56% for graphene/n-Si and retained approximately 90% of initial efficiency after 75 ambient-exposure days, versus approximately 29% for PEDOT:PSS/n-Si.
watch_item: The abstract reports only 75 days of ambient aging; longer-term durability and scalable, defect-free graphene integration remain to be established.
paper_title: Synergistic Graphene and PEDOT:PSS Layers on Silicon for Enhanced Efficiency and Stability in Schottky Junction Solar Cells
